acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Dockerfile exists for backend with multi-stage build (build + production stages)
Dockerfile exists for frontend with multi-stage build optimized for Next.js
docker-compose.yml orchestrates all services (backend, frontend, postgres)
Environment variables are configurable via .env file
Database migrations run automatically on container startup
Health checks are configured for all services in docker-compose
Volume mounts preserve database data between restarts
Developers can run docker-compose up and access the full application
Production build creates optimized images <500MB (backend) and <200MB (frontend)

doc.title: Project Architecture
doc.snippet: Defines monorepo structure with docker/ directory containing docker-compose.yml, Dockerfile.api, Dockerfile.web, and init.sql. Specifies service ports: Backend (3001), Frontend (3000), Database (5432).

doc.title: Epic 1 Technical Specification
doc.snippet: Provides detailed Docker Compose configuration examples with health checks, multi-stage Dockerfile patterns for API and frontend, database initialization script for pgvector extension, and environment variable templates.

doc.title: Epic Definitions
doc.snippet: DevOps engineer wants Docker containers for backend, frontend, and database with docker-compose orchestration so the application can be deployed consistently across environments.

doc.title: Previous Story (1.4)
doc.snippet: Next.js 15.5.6 configured with output: standalone for optimized Docker builds. Frontend runs on port 3000, API client configured for localhost:3001. TypeScript strict mode enabled.

artifact.reason: Existing Docker Compose setup with PostgreSQL (pgvector), API, and Web services including health checks and networking
Existing API Dockerfile with builder and production stages, non-root user, dumb-init signal handling
Existing Web Dockerfile with deps, builder, runner stages for Next.js standalone output
Database migration entry point script that runs prisma migrate deploy on container startup
Health check endpoint returning JSON with status, timestamp, services health, and version
Prisma schema with PostgreSQL provider and pgvector extension configuration
Next.js configuration with standalone output mode for optimized Docker builds
Turborepo build pipeline configuration with dependency tracking and caching
pnpm workspace configuration defining monorepo structure
Docker environment template with database, API, and web configuration variables

constraints.constraint: Multi-stage Docker builds required to minimize final image size
Non-root user in production containers for security
pnpm workspaces must be respected in Docker builds
Next.js standalone output mode for optimized container size
Prisma migrations must run automatically on API startup
Health checks for all services in docker-compose
Service dependencies via depends_on with health conditions
Services communicate via Docker internal network using service names
NEXT_PUBLIC_* variables baked in at build time

interface.name: Health Check Endpoint
interface.signature: GET /health -> { status: string, timestamp: string, services: { database: string }, version: string }

interface.name: Database Migration
interface.signature: prisma migrate deploy (production) / prisma migrate dev (development)

interface.name: Build Pipeline
interface.signature: turbo run build -> types first, then api/web in parallel

tests.standards: The project uses Vitest for API testing with @vitest/ui for interactive test runner. Tests should be co-located with source code or in __tests__ directories. Integration tests for Docker should verify service health, inter-service communication, data persistence, and environment variable loading. Docker tests are manual verification via curl commands and docker-compose ps/logs.

ideas.idea: Verify API Dockerfile builds successfully with docker build command
Verify Web Dockerfile builds successfully with standalone output
Test docker-compose up starts all three services
Verify .env file variables are loaded by checking container env
Test migrations run by checking database schema after fresh start
Verify health checks pass with docker-compose ps showing healthy status
Test persistence by creating data, restarting, and verifying data exists
Full stack test: docker-compose up, access frontend, verify API connectivity
Measure image sizes with docker images command, optimize if >targets
